transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Solutions); Diego Marquez (Stratacore), Hannah Lee (Stratacore), Elliot Park (Stratacore)

Summary: quick partner intro. Stratacore is a regional GPU + cloud provider focused on telco and edge customers. They want to understand Redwood's partner program, deployment options (private / dedicated), security posture, and benchmark expectations. SE dug into runtime, quantization, and routing. Action items were agreed to share security docs and scope a benchmark pilot.

Topics: partner program, deployment models (private vs dedicated vs hosted), security (SOC2, KMS, VPC), benchmarks and cost model, go-to-market motions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro \- I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Diego Marquez: Hi Maya, thanks. Diego here \- head of cloud partnerships at Stratacore. We run a mix of GPU instances tuned for telco/edge verticals.
[00:15] Hannah Lee: Hannah from partnerships, and Elliot on the line, our systems lead.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Great to meet you all. Quick agenda: partner intro from Redwood, high-level product fit, security and deployment options, and then dig into benchmarking and go-to-market. Sound good?
[00:29] Diego: Yep, that's perfect. We're early exploring strategic partners to add a managed inference offering on top of our infra. A few things: enterprise customers asking for VPC or on‑prem style controls, compliance, and predictable latency for streaming use cases.
[00:42] Maya: Totally. At a high level Redwood runs hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. Many partners like you integrate at the dedicated/private layer and resell or co-sell.
[00:55] Elliot Park: Can you clarify differences between dedicated and private? We've had customers ask specifically about on-prem air-gapped support.
[01:03] Liam: Sure. Dedicated in our terminology is reserved GPU pools that we operate for a customer with strong isolation and SLAs. Private is when the control plane can be handed to the customer \u2014 VPC connectors, optional air-gapped on‑prem package, KMS/HSM integrations. For air-gapped scenarios we ship an appliance and a private control-plane deployment model. Note: some of the words in the docs are slightly different but that's the gist.
[01:22] Diego: How heavy is the private deployment? Our ops folks worry about maintenance and upgrades.
[01:28] Priya Rao: From a partner perspective, we support managed private deployments where Redwood handles upgrades, or we can hand operational playbooks to partners who want full control. We also have a lightweight VPC connector for customers that want to keep workloads inside their network but use Redwood control plane.
[01:44] Elliot: For benchmarking, our infra uses custom PCIe-attached NVMe and mixed Tesla/Ampere GPUs. Typical request: run Llama-3-70B type loads and some lower-latency 7B models for chat. Any quantization recommendations?
[01:58] Liam: Yes. We typically recommend INT8/4-bit quant profiles for the 70B family where quality permits \u2014 Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles based on workload and target latency. For latency-sensitive chat on 7B, FP16 or 4-bit + kernel optimizations. Also routing policies can fallback to smaller models to keep tail latency.
[02:18] Diego: Are there kernel-level dependencies on Nvidia Triton or anything proprietary? Our stack is mostly native containers with k8s, but some customers want proprietary runtimes.
[02:27] Liam: Our runtime is GPU-optimized and we have compatibility layers. We don't require Triton; we ship a runtime that selects kernels and compiles where beneficial. There are still some hardware-specific kernel selections for Ampere vs Hopper but it's handled in our compilation layer.
[02:41] Hannah: On the security front \u2014 SOC2, SSO, RBAC \u2014 customers ask for SAML + SCIM and audit logs. Does Redwood have those?
[02:49] Maya: Yes. Redwood provides SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and audit logs. We also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We'll share the SOC2 summary and a short security whitepaper after this call.
[03:05] Elliot: For the KMS flow, do you support customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) and on-prem HSM?
[03:13] Liam: Yes \u2014 we support cloud KMS integrations and have an HSM integration path for private deployments. There are some nuances in air-gapped setups but we can document patterns.
[03:21] Diego: Commercially, we're thinking about reseller model vs joint go-to-market. We also want clear guidance on revenue splits and support SLAs for Dedicated.
[03:31] Maya: Absolutely \u2014 from partners we offer reseller agreements and co‑sell frameworks. We'll loop in GTM and legal to scope MSA terms. For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed latency and uptime tiers; pricing depends on reserved capacity and model families.
[03:45] Hannah: Any competitor callouts to be aware of? Some of our customers compare to AWS/Vertex and also smaller inference vendors.
[03:53] Maya: We typically position Redwood as production-first inference with flexible deployment modes and cost-aware controls. Competitors like cloud providers have deep infra but lack unified serving across private/dedicated/hosted; inference vendors may not have the same ops/observability.
[04:07] Elliot: Technical question: what's the typical per-token latency on 7B and 70B on your dedicated nodes? Ballpark numbers are fine.
[04:16] Liam: Ballpark: 7B FP16 token p50 ~8–12ms on a single high-frequency GPU; 70B depends on sharding \u2014 p50 for streaming is often in the 80–150ms range with optimized kernels and KV cache. Those numbers vary heavily with sequence length and batching. We'll run an actual benchmark on your exact hardware for accurate numbers.
[04:36] Diego: Sounds good. For the benchmark, we can provide instance types and some sample prompts. We want to validate both latency and cost per token.
[04:44] Liam: Great \u2014 please send the workload and we'll produce a benchmark runbook. Also we'll need access details to spin up a test environment (or we can run tests on our Dedicated infra if you prefer).
[04:58] Hannah: On integration, what's the typical onboarding timeline for partners doing a private deployment?
[05:04] Priya: For managed private deployments with Redwood handling orchestration, onboarding is typically 6–10 weeks depending on compliance requirements. For partner-managed, it can be longer.
[05:13] Diego: Anything else we should prep? Elliot: We'll gather the instance types and sample data.
[05:18] Maya: Perfect. Recap of next steps: 1) Maya sends partner intro + portal link, 2) Liam shares SOC2 + KMS notes, 3) Elliot provides benchmark workloads, 4) Diego to confirm regions and pilot customers, 5) schedule technical benchmark session (SE-led).
[05:36] Diego: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:38] Maya: Thanks \u2014 we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[05:42] (call ends)

References mentioned: Redwood partner portal (link: https://redwood.example/partners \u2014 placeholder), SOC2 summary (link: docx/pdf placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (link: internal sheet placeholder).
